newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Montenegrin court bans president from re-election.
newsitem.headline: Montenegrin court bans president from re-election.

text.p: The constitutional court of Montenegro on Thursday dealt a bitter blow to a hardline faction of the ruling DPS party by banning its candidate, current head of state Momir Bulatovic, from the autumn presidential race.
Political tensions increased after the Montenegro Electoral Commission earlier this week cleared President Bulatovic to run for the October 5 elections.

This meant he would take on Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic although they are both in the ruling Democratic Party of Socialists. The move violated the law that one party can have only one presidential candidate.

One DPS faction, headed by Djukanovic, engineered Bulatovic's removal last month from the post of DPS president, accusing him of taking orders from Serbia, the other, more populous and powerful republic in federal Yugoslavia.
Bulatovic is believed to be close to Slobodan Milosevic, the strongman former president of Serbia who has just taken over as federal president.
Djukanovic was confirmed as DPS candidate two weeks before Bulatovic.
Both factions claim rights to the name and assets of the party.
"The court decision is final," a senior source close to the Election Commission told Reuters on Thursday.
"Bulatovic's options are now limited to two - he can either run as an independent candidate or register his faction as a new party," the source said.
Analysts said in both cases Bulatovic was doomed to failure judging by the current state of public opinion which gave Djukanovic a strong lead.

The Djukanovic group feels that the reluctance of socialist, authoritarian Serbia to undertake democratic and free-market reforms is penalising reform-minded Montenegro by prolonging Yugoslavia's international isolation.
Bulatovic's faction accuses its foes under Djukanovic of plotting secession from Yugoslavia.
